name: Drought
value: El Niño drought risk; no harvest failure
summary: El Niño threatens a hotter, drier South African summer; record maize harvest and stocks cushion it
state: Forecasters expect a drier, hotter South African summer into early 2027 under an intense El Niño, with farmers planning 4.5 million hectares of summer crops, 2% less than last season; a record 17.7 million tonne maize harvest and about 2.4 million tonnes of stocks offer a cushion (Daily Maverick, 2 Nov). The AMIS Crop Monitor of 3 Sep reported drought in parts of Europe, Ukraine, the US Corn Belt, southern India, Thailand and Queensland. No harvest failure in a major exporter was found as of 8 Nov.
for_you: Southern African farming households and food-importing countries are the most exposed if rains fail. Effects on harvests would mostly show up from early 2027.
rubric_hit: Watch: severe drought in a major crop region (AMIS, 3 Sep); no major exporter's harvest failure or famine-driving drought confirmed

sources.title: Daily Maverick — El Niño threatens SA's crops but ample maize stocks cushion the blow
GEOGLAM — Crop Monitor for AMIS, September 2026

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
